model_result.answer_summary: A valid PL2 is the neutral bis(phosphatidyl) phosphate diester of symmetric 1,3-propanediol, with the two diacylglycerol stereocentres having the same handedness; its mirror has both handednesses reversed. PL3 is the physiological monoanion RCOO-CH2-CH(OCOR)-CH2-O-P(=O)(O-)-O-CH2CH3, together with its mirror enantiomer. The PL2 count is 255 - 13 + 12 = 254, and PL3 has hydrolysis coefficient m = 4.
assumptions: Standard closed-shell valences C=4, H=1, O=2, and phosphate P=5 are used to count sigma-plus-pi bond order.
The source's three equimolar reductive-ozonolysis pieces correspond to two C=C bonds in the acyclic fatty acid dependency.
Complete hydrolysis reverses the four carboxylate-ester and relevant phosphate-ester condensations shown by the constructed graphs.
Conventional skeletal-formula hydrogens are implicit, and each R pseudoatom denotes the common hydrocarbon residue requested by the prompt.
source_gaps: The prompt asks for a creative construction and gives no uniqueness criterion; the result proves a satisfying witness, not uniqueness.

The comparative phrase 'more symmetrical' is not assigned a point-group metric in the source. The formalization proves the concrete nontrivial involutive side exchange of the proposed PL2 instead of inventing such a metric.
